name: Sammy Kershaw
notes: The George Jones lineage on 90s radio — the decade's most explicit honky-tonk-weeper voice, and the entry states where the identity lives: "BPM 36–147 … the identity is the slow band, 66–84, with a mid-shuffle cluster at 106–126 and only two fast cuts". bpm.mode is therefore 79 ("Anywhere But Here"), not the arithmetic centre, and swing is set at 0.72 because the section's own grammar puts the slow 12/8 weeper near a 3:1 ratio. The drums follow the entry line by line: "the slow material is a written-out 12/8 with brushes or cross-stick, kick on 1 and 3, and the snare entering only at the chorus; the mid cluster runs a shuffled two-beat with the lope on a closed hat", cut by a producer (Buddy Cannon) "whose board keeps the kit small and dry". So the kick is pinned to 2 on the two-beat anchors with syncopation 0.05, the ghost stroke falls to 0.16 (the snare is barely there in the verses), the velocity tiers drop to 94–114 over 66–84, the rim lane carries the cross-stick and the inherited ride lane drops to 1–4 hits at −9 dB. Fills move out to 8/16 bars and transitions.fillBeforeSection is false because the entry is explicit: "no bridges on the weepers, no key changes, no dynamic escalation — the record stays at one intensity, which is the opposite of the `country-pop` power-ballad staging". Harmony is the entry's own — I–IV–V with V7, ii–V turnarounds on the weepers, twelve-bar frames on the barroom cuts — and the harmonic rhythm is weighted to two bars per chord for the slow band. The vocal is the documented "hard, cracked baritone with a pronounced downward slide off phrase ends, narrow range, low syllabic density, long held notes with a slow wide vibrato": a descend-heavy contour at 0.55, endVariation on, 48–69. The counter is the entry's stated co-lead — "pedal steel is the co-lead — long sustained bends answering every vocal phrase" — at a high density ratio an octave above. ⚠ INFERRED: swing.amount, all velocity tiers, ghost probability and vel, hat/percs densities and the counter's ratio; the section's swing-ratio percentages are marked [LOW-CONF] by their own author and the per-track BPM readings are bpmdatabase values, [LOW-CONF] as a class. The research also marks the harmony as generalised from the honky-tonk frame [LOW-CONF].
